descriptionChirho: To become discouraged, faint-hearted, or weary in the face of difficulty or prolonged effort. All six NT occurrences carry the same core meaning of spiritual or emotional exhaustion despite varying orthography (engk-/egk- forms). Used in 2 Cor 4:1,16 (we do not lose heart in ministry), Gal 6:9 (let us not grow weary in doing good), 2 Thess 3:13 (do not tire of doing right), Luke 18:1 (parable urging prayer without losing heart), Eph 3:13 (do not be discouraged by tribulations). Cross-linguistically uniform: Arabic nafshalu/nakillu (fail/flag), French se-decourager throughout, Spanish desmayar/cansar/desfallecer, Hebrew nilim/yitvaesh (weary/despair), Korean naksimhaji (not lose heart). No genuine polysemy exists; the four auto-clusters merely reflect inflectional variation (present indicative, present infinitive, aorist subjunctive, present subjunctive).
